decisions.reason: Organic sliced ham fits the firm's strategic push into organic lines, uses existing production and retail channels at low marginal cost, and no evidence of failure has emerged, so the option is worth keeping open.
Organic Kasseler is a low-cost extension of the core range that supports the organic strategy, and without negative signals keeping it on the shelf remains cheap.
Organic pepper salami builds on the firm's maturation capacity and organic ambitions, and its low holding cost justifies keeping it while demand is still being revealed.

The exotic teriyaki aspic is a riskier niche item for serviced deli counters, whose sales likely suffered during the pandemic, but it is still cheap to produce in small batches, so it is kept for now despite an elevated chance of being dropped.

Fennel salami was prominent enough to get its own page and is a regional-style specialty with low incremental cost, so the firm keeps the option open, though flavour variants rotate fairly often in this market.
A classic liver pâté with veal sits squarely in the established offer, carries little risk and low maintenance cost, and is likely to sustain steady demand.
